What did complete, before the failure, are two parsed events on the same operation stream: event 1 (control_catchup) with stale_suffix=false, old_last_after=55, applied 55 = leader commit 55 (comparison 0 outcome holds), and event 3 (case_nonmonotonic_stall) with snapshot_index=45 < old_last_before=223, applied frozen at 45 while leader commit 55, stalled=true, isolated_caught_up=false (comparison 1 outcome violated, valid witness index 3). The monotonic scenario ran (its [CA] log line reports snapshot_index=45, oldLastBefore=222, leaderCommit=55) but emitted no CA_EVENT before the test panicked in the harness helper cluster.Close() after its shutdown-timeout timer fired (testing.go:307), i.e. a harness cleanup timeout, not a target assertion. No monotonic endpoint was measured, so the discriminator between retained above-snapshot bytes and the cached last-log state is not decided by this run.
counterevidence: Native local runs of the same harness (before submission, not a formal receipt) showed the monotonic scenario stalling identically (old_last_after=223, applied=45, stalled=true). This is why the question is worth resuming, but it is not retained execution evidence and is not used as a conclusion.

limitations: Concrete resume condition: emit the monotonic scenario's result event (or explicitly Shutdown and await each Raft before cluster.Close) so the measurement precedes cleanup, then re-run this exact harness as a fresh successor; a completed receipt with the monotonic comparison then decides the gap.
